title: A unified quantum random walk model for internal crystal effects in dynamical diffraction
summary: The theory of dynamical diffraction (DD) in perfect crystals is the backbone of high-precision neutron and X-ray diffraction experiments, enabling accurate determination of crystal structure factors and the realization of perfect crystal interferometers. In practice, however, real crystals exhibit deformations and imperfections, including surface roughness, defects, temperature gradients, angled crystal faces, and curvature, that degrade interferometer performance and are difficult to model using conventional DD theory, particularly in complex geometries.
